doc.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011

title: The Brubeck children and growing up with music
summary: Sons Matthew and Darius and music around them, and the adjustment of having a famous father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And your children gravitated. The cellist, is Michael?
Matthew said when asked about making a living as a musician he said, “I didn’t know there was any other way.”

I know. I think that’s the way all of them felt, that music was just around them all the time when they were growing up, and I know I’ve heard our oldest one, Darius, explain, it just seemed like the grown-ups were having so much fun and they were just playing and it just seemed like something that, “That’s what I want to do when I grow up.” And they all started taking lessons when they were pretty young and they drifted from one instrument to another and finally settled on what they wanted to play. And they’re all good musicians.
Did they have a sense early on that their — I’m not sure how to ask this — that their father was a well-known public figure? Did they understand that?

I think that that is when you are an adolescent and in your early years I think that is an issue that you have to adjust to, and again, our oldest son has talked about it more I think than most of the others, and he probably felt it more than the others, because he was an adolescent just at the time that Dave’s fame was at its greatest. And he was saying that it took him a while to realize while I’m not my father, that there is no reason for me to be comparing myself with my father. I have my own positives and negatives, and he has, but he said it took a while for him. Because also he’s the pianist of the group and I think that made it doubly difficult.
